messages:
emma: noticed some GPU nodes failing autoscaler checks this morning, saw a boatload of 404-like errors from node-problem-detector logs
omar: any recent mesh/egress changes?
li: pushed a small egress deny rule to egress-gateway last night to lock down external hosts, nothing else AFAIK
sre-bot: alert: node/i-0abcd1234 metadata-fetch-failure repeated on eu-west-1-gpu-pool (x6)
emma: digging in — nodes report missing instance-profile tags so cluster-autoscaler treats them as non-eligible. curl to IMDS times out when run from pod sidecar.
omar: wait — IMDS is 169.254.169.254 right? could our sidecar be intercepting that? :thinking_face:
li: I found iptables redirect rule we added for the sidecar:
```
-A PREROUTING -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j REDIRECT --to-ports 15001
-A OUTPUT -p tcp -m owner --uid-owner 1337 -j RETURN
```
The rule set was too broad and got applied before the EXEMPT rule for link-local.
emma: repro from pod: `curl -v --connect-timeout 1 http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/` -> connection reset. From host `curl` works.
natalie: so sidecar is catching IMDS traffic and egress policy on the gateway denies 169.254.169.254 because we treat link-local as external in the deny list.
omar: that explains why kubelet/auth can't refresh creds -> IAM tokens unavailable -> node loss of labels -> autoscaler skips GPU nodes. Ouch.
infra-oncall: temporary mitigation: add iptables rule to bypass redirect for 169.254.169.254 before PREROUTING redirect. Also allow IMDS in egress-gateway config as a host exception.
li: patch ready: add `-d 169.254.169.254/32 -j ACCEPT` before REDIRECT and add exception in egress-gateway ACL. I'll push to canary.
emma: can we also update the sidecar init script to create an explicit bypass for link-local addresses by default? We keep hitting different cloud metadata endpoints (aws/azure/gcp) so safer to whitelist 169.254.169.254 and  metadata IPs per cloud.
mar: (not in thread) quick question: do we need to worry about SSRF or exfil risk if we allow IMDS from pods?
omar: yes, but we already enforce pod-iam policies and metadata access is sensitive. We should allow only node-level access, not pod-level. Best is to bypass only on OUTPUT chain for host namespace traffic, not redirect pod traffic. In our case the redirect was too early and hit pod-originated calls too.
infra-oncall: rollout plan: li will deploy iptables bypass to canary GPU pool (eu-west-1) then update egress-gateway ACL to permit 169.254.169.254 from node subnets only, not all pods. Monitor cluster-autoscaler and node labels for 30m.
li: deployed to canary at 1835043300, added rule and gateway exception.
emma: after change, `curl` from a previously-affected pod returns IAM role name within 2s. cluster-autoscaler marked 2 GPU nodes healthy again. :thumbsup:
omar: followup: we should add an automated unit test for init-container iptables ordering, and document the default bypass for link-local addresses in devdocs.
natalie: filing docs ticket and a small design note on scope of exceptions (node-only vs pod).
infra-oncall: closing incident if stable for 1h. tagging cost-impact: medium (temporary missed scale-ups cost us ~2-3 hours of cold GPUs), root cause: overly-broad iptables redirect + restrictive egress ACL.
emma: thanks all — good catch.
li: will open PR to change init script and add unit test.
infra-oncall: reminder: if you hit metadata issues, first try `nsenter --target $(pidof kubelet) --mount -- bash -c 'curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/'` to confirm host vs pod behavior.
